exposure: congenital uterine anomalies (septate, bicornuate, unicornuate, didelphic uterus)
cohort: The study included 45 pregnancies complicated by congenital uterine anomalies (septate, bicornuate, unicornuate, didelphic uterus) and compared them to pregnancies with normal uteri.
finding: Congenital uterine anomalies were significantly associated with a higher incidence of fetal malpresentation and abnormal placental cord insertion.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was more likely in the major uterine anomaly group compared to the minor anomaly and normal uterus groups.
